content: Example services use the vanilla org.openapi.generator plugin with generatorName=spring, interfaceOnly=true, useSpringBoot3=true, useTags=true, skipDefaultInterface=true. The spec generates *Api interfaces + DTO models; we write the @RestController impls. Generated sources go to build/generated and are wired into the main source set; compileJava dependsOn openApiGenerate. Keep spec <-> controllers <-> DTOs in sync.

name: Hierarchical REST paths mirror the resource tree
description: Nest URLs to reflect the resource hierarchy: /catalogs/{id}/categories/{id}/products/{id}. Validate each ancestor exists and that the child belongs to it (findByIdAndParentId) so cross-parent access returns 404, not someone else's data. This nesting is also what the ABAC hierarchical-authorization pattern keys off.

content: Map JPA column types to match the entity exactly, validated against REAL Postgres. char(3) becomes bpchar and fails Hibernate ddl-auto=validate against a String field expecting varchar — use varchar(n). timestamptz needs @TimeZoneStorage(NATIVE) on OffsetDateTime. Run schema validation under Testcontainers (real Postgres), never H2, so these mismatches surface in the build.

name: REST API conventions + design-review baseline (both example services)
description: Both example services share one REST convention set, now pinned in docs/guides/REST-API-DESIGN.md + reviewed in docs/code-review/REST-API-DESIGN-REVIEW.md. Conventions: spec-first OpenAPI (org.openapi.generator, interfaceOnly, controller implements <Api>); /api/v1 path versioning; plural nouns; ownership-nesting <=3 levels (catalog->category->product hits 3); custom op as noun sub-resource (POST /teams/{id}/transfer-ownership); PUT-not-PATCH full-replace; ApiError{status,message,timestamp} as application/json. Status rules: 400=Bean-Validation/syntax, 422=domain-rule (tag dict / role-subset), 409=state-conflict/immutable, 503=fail-closed dependency outage (tag dict unreachable -> reject, never store untagged), no 401 (gateway authenticates; deny=403). Authz per endpoint = one of three: type-level @OpaPreAuthorize, load-then-check (only getCategory, because tags live only on CategoryEntity), partial-eval list filter (empty list not full table on no-grant). Public/internal split: /api/v1/** authenticated; /internal/** permitAll BUT network-isolated, never gateway-fronted (deployment invariant, not code). REVIEW VERDICT: consistent, no fail-open found. Gaps=maturity targets, not bugs: (1 Medium) no RFC-7807 problem+json / stable errorCode -> top publication item; (2 Low) no Location on 201; (3) getCatalog/getProduct annotation-only vs getCategory load-then-check is intentional (doc it); (4) some user-svc mutations (UserController, POST /teams) authenticated-but-not-ABAC-gated = bootstrap seam, add intent comments; (5) no pagination = documented demo limit; (6) no actions/pageActions = Phase 6 action-enrichment.

title: Phase 5.9 error contract: RFC-7807 problem+json + library-owned errorCode vocabulary (ADR 0011)
rationale: Settled via grill-me 2026-06-09 and pinned by ADR 0011. Five forks: (1) depth = the minimal additive RFC-7807 superset (type/title/status/detail/instance + errorCode/timestamp extensions), NO hosted type registry. (2) clean replacement of the legacy ApiError status/message/timestamp shape, message renamed to detail, content type flips to application/problem+json (no external consumers pre-publication, so a clean break is free). (3) vocabulary = an ApiErrorCode INTERFACE plus a LibraryErrorCode enum in opa-abac-spring-security for the failures the library raises, each example service ships its OWN enum implementing the same interface (a Java enum cannot be subclassed, so the contract slot is the interface). (4) SEMANTIC granularity: one code per distinct client-actionable failure, not one per HTTP status. (5) errorCode is a first-class TYPED enum member of each spec ProblemDetail schema so the generated client is typed, which is why the library ships its own small ProblemDetail DTO rather than Spring built-in ProblemDetail whose properties map is untyped. A non-obvious real-code catch the slice-planner surfaced: 403 from OpaPreAuthorize is rendered by Spring Security default today, so the T1 advice base must explicitly map AccessDeniedException to ACCESS_DENIED 403 or 403s never become problem+json. Pagination split to its OWN slice Phase 5.95 sequenced 5.9 then 5.95 then Phase 6 so action enrichment lands on an already-paginated 7807-clean surface. Out of scope: hosted registry, actions metadata (Phase 6), any authorization behavior change.
